findings.section: HS-39 give_up and self placement; EC-HS-56/57; AC-HS-147(c)
findings.finding: Internal contradiction in the give_up/self plate placement rule: the plate is 'never withheld', yet 'if none passes, UI_PLACEMENT_WITHHELD increments and that is a build-gate defect, not a runtime fallback'. Nothing says what is drawn at runtime when none of the four candidates fits (an odd camera clamp or a custom H). The exit for user ruling D7 (give up and reload) would silently vanish, and an implementer has no defined behaviour.
findings.fix: Add a deterministic last resort: if no candidate clears the exclusion rectangles, draw the plate at the first candidate that clears the chest keep-out and the safe margin, ignoring only the strip/panel/rail exclusion (z-ordered above them for the DOWNED duration), and count UI_PLACEMENT_FALLBACK. Keep the build-gate AC that the fallback is never hit on the D.8 picture list.

findings.section: UI Requirements item 2 (l.1559); registry bottom_row_fit.output
findings.finding: Item 2 still says 'The sizing constraint is 100 HUD px per side (panel and rail each)' and 'H_default and H_default + 1 are offered on every picture in the D.8 table'. That contradicts D.8: the 100 x 44 box is withdrawn, ROW is 144 and COLUMN 74, and ROW offers only {3} on k_auto = 2 pictures. The registry bottom_row_fit.output still lists the COLUMN-at-50 % sets ({3,4} at 720p, {3..6} at 1080p) with an in-file note that they are stale (revised 2026-10-27, unrefreshed).
findings.fix: Rewrite item 2 as 'each side surface must fit side_avail(P_w, H) of D.8 for the chosen arrangement; offered() is the per-arrangement table'. Refresh the registry output into two rows (ROW and COLUMN) copied from the D.8 arrangement table and drop the 'stale until recomputed' comment.

findings.section: HS-30 (l.261), Cross-References / OQ-HS-61 (l.1953), CF-HS-... (l.1362); Last Verified header
findings.finding: R20 sweep leftovers: 'the creative-director's recommendation, still subject to user confirmation' remains at four sites (l.245, 261, 1362, 1953) and R20 says re-mark as 'confirmed 2026-10-28 - delegated ruling R20'. The header still shows 'Last Verified: 2026-10-26'. A related sentence at l.1917 and OQ-HS-3's gap bullet says the atlas and needle strips have 'no memory budget stated anywhere; none is invented here', but this GDD now states HUD_MEM_CEILING_MB 8 [PH] (Tuning Knobs l.1108, AC-HS-92).
findings.fix: Re-mark the four sites with the R20 wording. Update Last Verified. Rewrite the l.1917 gap to 'HUD_MEM_CEILING_MB 8 [PH] is unmeasured; pending spike S2'. Grep for the old phrases after editing (G3).

findings.section: HS-6; OQ-HS-18; K16; registry input_view (source: interaction-system.md)
findings.finding: One read still has two names. The Controller publishes confirm_view = {b, mode, armed, pressed, released, give_up_live}. The registry entry is named input_view and its source: is interaction-system.md, but its rule text says the owner is the Controller; Interaction has 16 'input_view' mentions and the HUD uses confirm_view. Under G1 the publisher names it.
findings.fix: Set the registry entry's name to confirm_view and its source to player-controller-input.md (keep input_view as a 'was' comment). Route the rename to Interaction's writer (IA-41 and the 16 mentions). Then drop the 'names still to reconcile' clauses from OQ-HS-18, K16 and the Gaps bullet.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-HS-46, AC-HS-51 (review-only)
findings.finding: Both are 'review' ACs with nothing a tester can pass or fail: AC-HS-46 'WHEN reviewed THEN the HUD never draws the true value beside it, never shows a lie count, and never caches a Perceived across frames'; AC-HS-51 'WHEN reviewed THEN it is SCANNER_LIE_STAGE ... not READING_LIE_STAGE'.
findings.fix: AC-HS-46 (auto, RESERVED): stub Filter returns a lying Perceived for one key; render 600 frames; a scene-tree and pixel diff against the honest run differs only inside that reading's rectangle; no node or string carries a lie count; the Perceived record address differs per frame (no caching). AC-HS-51 (lint): the scanner slot's code path references SCANNER_LIE_STAGE and never READING_LIE_STAGE; a stub at stage 2 leaves the scanner honest and at stage 3 lets it lie.

findings.section: Game Feel step 4 / GF-HS-3 (l.1455)
findings.finding: Stale CONFIRM_HOLD_S range. The progress row says '2.25 to 4.5 ticks across the Controller's 0.6-1.2 s range'; the registry (and this GDD's own table 3) says 0.6-1.9 s. The per-px step across the real range is 36/16 = 2.25 to 114/16 = 7.125 ticks (0.8 s default = 3.0, Chart Table's 1.6 s = 6.0).
findings.fix: Change the sentence to '2.25 to 7.125 ticks per px across the Controller's 0.6-1.9 s range' and recompute any AC that cites 4.5.

findings.section: HS-26 and EC-HS-50 (motion_mode dispatch)
findings.finding: The dispatch lists HONEST, GLIDE, TICK, STALE and RETURN, but the Filter's motion_mode enum also has BREATH (state glyphs and housing appearance), and nothing says what any slot draws for BREATH or an unknown value. An implementer must invent a default.
findings.fix: Add: 'BREATH and any unknown motion_mode draw HONEST and increment hud_unknown_motion_mode (BREATH is not used by any MVP HUD slot; the gleam breath of a state glyph is the Filter's leak_modes, not a dispatch branch).' Add a stub-Filter AC for an out-of-range value.

findings.section: Player Fantasy anchor table, Anti-pillar 4, Visual/Audio truth-channel table (l.1171-1197)
findings.finding: The DOWNED give_up plate is a new on-screen word ('Give up') and a new surface, but anti-pillar 4 still says the only text lines are the failed-write notice and first-frame line, the Player Fantasy has no DOWNED beat, and the truth-channel classification table has no row for hud_give_up_plate (HS-42(b) says 'truth, meta register' only in the rule text). Same for the self plate.
findings.fix: Add a DOWNED beat to the anchor-moment text (the exit is offered, never explained, no cause or countdown). Add a row 'give_up plate, self plate: A/meta, never lie-capable' to the truth-channel table. Amend anti-pillar 4 to read 'plate verbs and the two meta lines'.

findings.section: HS-43, EC-HS-39 (closed carry set); HS-37 self plate; AC-HS-67
findings.finding: The new self plate is not addressed by the carry rule. HS-43 says that while carrying, the only prompts are Drop plus three carry-admitted verbs, and 'nothing on any other world target'. Interaction's self_target forces prompt_state ENABLED (act_gate exempt) with no carry test, and begin_patch is BUSY while carrying (IA carry-admitted list excludes it). A welder in hand plus a carried module could draw a 'Patch suit' plate the sim will reject, which is a prompt lie. AC-HS-67 does not cover it.
findings.fix: Add to HS-43: 'the self plate is not drawn while carry_state is carrying' (HUD-side clause, one line, like the give_up_live clause), plus a clause in AC-HS-67. Ask Interaction's writer to make prompt_state HIDDEN for self_target while carrying so the HUD rule is a belt and braces check.

findings.section: HS-37 self plate; Game Feel / Playtest questions
findings.finding: By Interaction's rule the self-patch prompt is ENABLED for any actor holding the welder, whatever integrity_bp is, so with a welder in hand the HUD shows a 'Patch suit' plate (hollow keycap while walking, because patch is a CHANNEL verb) every time no world candidate has focus. That is a persistent plate popping in and out at the debounce (13 ticks) and min-cycle (20 ticks) limits, drawing from the 3-per-second flash budget in STRICT mode. It is an Interaction ruling, so the HUD has no defect, but no playtest question or HS-56 note covers its noise.
findings.fix: Add a playtest question (is a constant 'Patch suit' plate noise or a useful affordance?) and a fallback lever the HUD owns, e.g. draw the self plate only after the focus has been empty for N ticks, with N a [PH] knob, if the playtest says noisy.

findings.section: Tone and language (HUD_DEATH_WORDS)
findings.finding: The lint list is 'whole-word and stem'. A stem match on 'die' would also hit 'diesel', 'soldier' or 'studies'; 'revive' is denied 'because solo has none at MVP' although the Vertical Slice B revive verb would be linted out of existence.
findings.fix: State the stem rule as 'word-start prefix of a whole token, with an allow-list' and note that 'revive' lifts at Vertical Slice B (a dated entry in the list's data file).

findings.section: Sibling stale references (EM-22, Horror AC-59b)
findings.finding: Review 4 reported two siblings (Emitter State EM-22, Horror AC-59b) that describe the prompt as following lit(ref). I could not find a clear stale statement in either on this pass (EM-22 describes lit(ref) correctly; AC-59b was not located), so this item is unverified rather than closed.
findings.fix: When those two GDDs are next touched, confirm they say the HUD draws exactly where Interaction's prompt_state says and never queries lit(ref).

input.summary: Verdict: APPROVED, with 0 BLOCKING findings. The file is the largest GDD in the set (637 KB, 151 ACs). Of the review-4 items, the give_up/object-prompt co-existence rule, the D.15 example (466), the ship-alarm order (step 125, matching Graph D.11 Example B) and the R12 reference-machine text are fixed; the 14 other review-4 items were not touched, because this GDD had no blocker in the last fix pass. The new edits (give_up plate, self-patch plate, K43, AC-HS-147 to 150) agree with the Controller, Interaction and Graph; I checked AC-PCI-024, AC-PCI-145, `self_target`, IA-28, LS-13 (c) and the alarm_capable correction. Arithmetic I recomputed holds: D.1 (63 content, slack 13, 76 cap), the D.8 per-arrangement sets at 720p and 1080p, the HUD_NONGROUND allocation (2,304 = 1 % of 230,400), the D.2 admission example, and the give_up drain and fill figures (500 permille drains in 12 ticks; 500 permille fills 8 px). I found no implementation-wrong or impossible defect. The closest calls are both RECOMMENDED. First, AC-HS-145 is an automated, BLOCKING-gated criterion that is written to fail at 2.77:1 (R21 forbids leaving it open). Second, the unspecified runtime behaviour when no give_up placement fits, which could hide the exit D7 requires. The other changes needed are mostly stale text: four RESERVE_S sites (45-240 vs registry 63-240), the MARK_DUTY_PM range (duty above 531 at period 128 breaks the window proof), the Filter's missing suit.alarm key, AC-HS-147(c) testing H 2 (never offered), UI Requirements item 2, the OQ-HS-81 COLUMN lean, and R20 leftovers. The three new issues from this pass are the self plate under carry, the 'no memory budget' gap line, and the missing DOWNED/give_up row in the truth-channel table. Dependencies: every designed neighbour GDD exists; the undesigned ones (Avatar Presenter, Accessibility Settings, Input Rebinding, Crew Strip, Co-op Session, Chat, Onboarding) are R9 provisional and not blockers.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-HS-145; Open Questions OQ-HS-83; HS-20
findings.finding: AC-HS-145 is written to fail ('the criterion is expected to FAIL for Graphite lit #5C6670 on Ground (about 2.8:1)'), while Visual and UI gates are BLOCKING, so it would block every story touching the lamp-OFF outline, the mark's OFF outline, the dimmed notches and dead-source bands. findings.fix: Decide under R21 (preserve prior rulings, least new content): record a documented waiver for Graphite lit state-carrying strokes at 2.77:1, keeping the palette locked, and state the AC with an explicit exemption list so it passes. Put the 3:1 / 4.5:1 floors on every other glyph, numeral and text run; keep the Hull Grey move as the art-director's optional upgrade, not a precondition. Close OQ-HS-83 with a 'Resolved 2026-10-28 - delegated ruling R21' line.

findings.section: Open Questions OQ-HS-81; D.8 arr; Tuning Knobs
findings.finding: OQ-HS-81 still states 'The creative-director's lean (following the game-designer) is COLUMN-preserving-the-ceiling, so a sketch of COLUMN comes first'. The CD withdrew that lean on 2026-10-28 because COLUMN breaks P1 (the upper 70 % of the screen must stay HUD-free). D.8 itself correctly sets no default arrangement. Under R21 the ROW/COLUMN choice cannot be left without a default.
findings.fix: Rewrite the lean sentence: the CD's lean is ROW (keeps P1's upper 70 %), COLUMN is the fallback if the accessibility-specialist requires the 133 % H ceiling. Record the default as ROW under R21 (reason: preserves the P1 ruling and needs no new content), keep D.8 validating both arrangements, and make the UX-spec sketch ROW-first.

findings.section: D.3 (l.528-529), Tuning Knobs cited-knobs (l.1132), Cross-References table 3 (l.1667), OQ-HS-80(3) (l.1977); AC-HS-91
findings.finding: The HUD cites RESERVE_S as '90 (45-240)' at four sites. The registry (source suit-and-equipment.md) and Suit SE-6 say the range is 63-240 (build assertion A15). AC-HS-91 ('cited value equals registry value') fails literally on table 3. The text at l.1977 even proposes registering a bound the Suit has already registered. Unchanged since review 4 because this GDD had no blocker.
findings.fix: Change all four sites to 90 (63-240); in D.3 keep the three-digit-cell note, which holds anyway at 240. Rewrite OQ-HS-80(3) as 'done: Suit A5 and A15'. Add a one-line grep AC: no '45-240' appears in this file.

findings.section: D.2 / HS-23 / Tuning Knobs MARK_DUTY_PM; AC-HS-123; registry MARK_DUTY_PM
findings.finding: MARK_DUTY_PM is ranged 400-600, but the flash-window proof needs the OFF gap to be at least 60 ticks: gap = BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS x (1000 - duty)/1000 = 51 ticks at duty 600 and period 128. A window can then hold an orphan OFF edge plus the ON edge of one mark (2 counted events), plus 2 grid boundaries at g = 30, giving 4 > FLASH_MAX_PER_S 3. The default 500 is safe (gap 64), but the declared range includes failing values and the AC-HS-123 validator checks only HONEST_TICK_MS and u, not duty. The registry note says the range 'stands'.
findings.fix: Replace the literal range with a derived constraint: MARK_DUTY_PM <= 1000 - ceil_div(60000, BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS) (531 at 128, 500 at 120, 666 at 180), with a lower bound of about 400 for pulse readability. Add it to the AC-HS-123 validator list and to the registry MARK_DUTY_PM range text. Give a failing fixture: duty 600 at period 128 is rejected.

findings.section: HS-6 / HS-25 / OQ-HS-79(2) / OQ-HS-8; AC-HS-33(e); perception-filter.md
findings.finding: G6 GAP still open. The user-ruled D89 ship-alarm mark reads perceived(suit.alarm) as a sixth TRUTH-class key, and Suit SE-29 says it reaches the HUD through the Filter. perception-filter.md still has zero occurrences of 'suit.alarm' and its text says 'the five keys'. The Filter was not among the 10 GDDs revised in the last pass. The HUD is built against a stub, AC-HS-33(e) is 'provisional', and AC-HS-39 explicitly excludes the Filter definition from its pass line, so the alarm mark cannot be fed end to end. Under G6 the owner (Filter) adds the surface.
findings.fix: Route to the Filter's writer: add a sixth TRUTH-class SUIT_KEY(suit.alarm) with its lie stage pinned 'never', and state how the one bit sits in the Perceived record (e.g. displayed_pm 0 or 1000, motion_mode HONEST, never wrapped). Then drop 'provisional' from AC-HS-33(e) and OQ-HS-79(2).

findings.fix: Rewrite (c) to: 'for chest points at the picture centre and at 20 HUD px inside each of the four safe-margin edges, at every H in offered(P_w, P_h, arr) for both arrangements on each D.8 picture, one of above/below/right/left clears the 16-px keep-out, the 4-px margin and the strip/panel/rail rectangles, UI_PLACEMENT_WITHHELD never increments, and the plate rectangle never intersects the keep-out.' findings.fix: Replace the literal range with a derived constraint: MARK_DUTY_PM <= 1000 - ceil_div(60000, BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS) (531 at 128, 500 at 120, 666 at 180), with a lower bound of about 400 for pulse readability.
